title: RNA Extraction from Cells Encapsulated in Alginate Using Maxwell® RSC Plant RNA Kit
author: Helen Kearney
materials: Maxwell® RSC Plant RNA Kit cartridges

steps.title: Prepare Alginate Lyase Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the alginate lyase solution and store or warm as needed.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 2 mg alginate lyase powder per 1 mL solution needed.
Dissolve powder in PBS (or 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 6.3 for optimum activity).
Invert to mix or gently vortex.
Sterile filter the solution using a 0.2 µm pore filter and syringe.
Store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Warm in a 37°C water bath before use.

steps.title: Collect Encapsulated Samples
steps.instruction: Transfer encapsulated cells, spheroids, or organoids into a tube and determine total volume.

substeps.instruction: Transfer samples encapsulated in alginate norbornene hydrogel into an Eppendorf tube (a 1.5 mL tube with a tapered bottom is recommended).
Calculate total hydrogel volume (e.g., number of organoids multiplied by the volume of gel each is encapsulated in).
Spin down cells/spheroids/organoids at 300 g for 1 min to gather them at the bottom of the tube (adjust time/speed based on sample type; e.g., 300 g for 5 min for monolayer cultures).

steps.title: Digest Alginate Hydrogel
steps.instruction: Release cells/spheroids/organoids from the hydrogel using alginate lyase.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 20 U/mL alginate lyase solution to the total hydrogel volume in each Eppendorf.
Incubate in a 37 °C water bath for 10–15 min.
Invert the tube to check digestion progress; only cell pellet/free-spheroids/free-organoids should be visible at the bottom.
Remove the alginate lyase solution. If the hydrogel is not completely dissolved, replace with the same volume of fresh solution and repeat the digestion and incubation steps.

steps.title: Wash and Prepare Samples
steps.instruction: Clean the released samples and prepare for extraction.

substeps.instruction: Wash cells/spheroids/organoids twice with PBS to remove residual enzyme, spinning down at the same speed used for collection.
Either proceed directly to RNA extraction or snap-freeze samples in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Homogenization Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the Thiolglycerol/Homogenization buffer and keep on ice.

substeps.instruction: Mix 20 μL Thiolglycerol per 1 mL Homogenization buffer according to manufacturer's guidelines.

steps.title: Homogenize Samples
steps.instruction: Thaw and homogenize samples using the prepared buffer.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve samples and place on ice.
Immediately add 220 μL Thiolglycerol/Homogenization buffer.
Allow samples to thaw in buffer.
Gently invert samples twice (do not pipette, shake, or homogenize).
Keep samples cold on ice for 10 min.

steps.title: Lyse Samples
steps.instruction: Perform chemical lysis of the samples.

substeps.instruction: Add 220 μL lysis buffer to each sample.
Gently invert twice (do not pipette, shake, or homogenize).
Incubate at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Prepare RSC Cartridges
steps.instruction: Set up the Maxwell® RSC Plant RNA kit cartridges while samples incubate.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL DNase solution in the dedicated well/compartment.
Prepare elution tube with 50 µL nuclease-free water.
Place plunger in appropriate compartment.

steps.title: Clarify Lysed Sample
steps.instruction: Remove debris from the lysed sample via centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 400 μL lysed sample to a new Eppendorf tube.
Spin at 15,000 g for 2 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Perform Automated RNA Extraction
steps.instruction: Process the samples using the Maxwell® RSC instrument.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to the first well of the RSC cartridge, leaving behind any solid debris.
Run the Plant RNA kit protocol on the Maxwell® RSC instrument using the provided software.

steps.title: Quantify RNA Yield
steps.instruction: Recover RNA and measure concentration and purity.

substeps.instruction: Remove the RNA elution tubes from the instrument.
Measure RNA yield using a Spectrometer (for purity A260/A280 and A260/A230) or a Fluorometer (for accurate quantification of low yields or suboptimal purity).
